tools.blocked_reason:
BLOCKED — SURFACED 5/5 and CALLED 0/5, and the model was RIGHT not to call it.

It answered "there are no public books in the catalogue to open" and ended the turn. That is true about the tool it was given: catalog_list_public_books returns {"items": [], "total": 0}.

🔴 BUT THE STORE SAYS OTHERWISE. loreweave_sharing.sharing_policies holds 44 rows with visibility='public' (against 13 private and 1 unlisted). So 44 books are marked public and the public catalogue lists none of them.

A direct probe pins it further: catalog_get_book returns 'book not found' for the fixture's own private book, for an unknown id, AND for a book_id that IS marked public in sharing_policies. The refusal is uniform — which is correct, it is no existence oracle — and the catalogue projection is simply empty of everything.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE SHAPE IN THIS STRETCH, and that is why it is worth naming rather than filing as a quirk:
  * kg_add_nodes answers 'node ready'; kg_graph_query reports zero nodes (it projects nodes FROM EDGES, so an edgeless node is invisible)
  * memory_remember stores a fact; memory_search cannot find it until the project is indexed ('degraded': {'semantic': 'not_indexed'})
  * sharing_policies marks 44 books public; catalog_list_public_books returns 0
In all three the write side confirms and the read side that surfaces it returns nothing, and in all three THE MODEL'S 'it isn't there' WAS TRUE. The false absence belongs to the platform, and an author asking 'what public books are there' is told none while 44 are marked public.

Whether the catalogue is a projection that was never populated, or one that needs an explicit publish step beyond the sharing policy, is not established here — loreweave_catalog holds only catalog_runtime_state, so the listing is built elsewhere. Recorded as DQ-T38 rather than guessed at.

tools.falsifier: 🔴 THIS TOOL SPENDS — it enqueues a background job that DRAFTS with an LLM — so its card is NEVER approved and the measurement is what the card CARRIES, not what the job produces. REFUTED IF: a job is enqueued with NO confirm card, OR the model fills `args` with a coverage_limit or a targets list the author never mentioned — the author asked to enrich thin entities, not to bound or target the run — OR the reply describes the enrichment as DONE. Its own description says the job returns immediately and every generated proposal is QUARANTINED for human review, so 'I've enriched your lore' is wrong twice over: nothing is written and nothing is reviewed.

ship_audit.gate: EXERCISED — Tier A AND cost-bearing (it enqueues a job that DRAFTS with an LLM), card raised 5/5 with the store unchanged and no job enqueued. The card is the spend consent and it was never approved, which is the standing rule for a cost-bearing tool.
ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED by direct probe — and the nested args validate BEFORE the project lookup: an unknown project_id with incomplete args returns a Pydantic validation error naming the missing fields (args.embedding_model_ref among them) rather than a project refusal. Ordering worth knowing, not a defect: a caller fixing the project id would still have to fix the args.
ship_audit.empty_case: NOT REACHED — the probe could not get past args validation to see what an empty glossary does, so 'reports no gaps rather than enqueuing a job over nothing' is UNVERIFIED and recorded as such rather than claimed.
ship_audit.idempotency: NOT REACHED — the card is never approved, so no job existed to queue twice.
ship_audit.tenancy: NOT REACHED — the same args validation fires before the ownership check.
ship_audit.args_declaration: 🔴 WORTH RECORDING, because it corrected one of my own instruments. `args` carries no top-level description and the undeclared-required-args gate counted it as bare. It is not: it is a nested object arriving as a `$ref`, and the schema it points at opens 'Every field carries a Field(description=...) on purpose' and describes every field inside. The model plainly saw them — it called the tool 5/5 with a complete args object. The gate now follows a $ref; measured across the whole baseline this was the ONLY entry of that shape, 1 in 105.

_dq.DQ-T38:
The PUBLIC CATALOGUE lists nothing while 44 books are marked public. Measured batch 40: loreweave_sharing.sharing_policies holds 44 rows with visibility='public', and catalog_list_public_books returns {"items": [], "total": 0}. catalog_get_book returns 'book not found' even for a book_id that IS marked public in sharing_policies — uniformly, the same answer a private or unknown id gets, so it is no existence oracle but it is also no help.

Consequence for an author: asked what public books exist, the assistant truthfully reports none, and any book they believe they published is unreachable through the catalogue tools.

NOT DIAGNOSED FURTHER HERE, deliberately: loreweave_catalog holds only catalog_runtime_state, so the listing is built somewhere else, and whether this is a projection that was never populated or a publish step beyond the sharing policy is a question about that pipeline. Guessing at it would be the sixth prose-shaped hypothesis this loop has had to retract.

SAME SHAPE as D-EDGELESS-NODE-INVISIBLE-TO-THE-GRAPH-READ (batch 33) and D-STORED-BUT-UNFINDABLE-UNTIL-INDEXED (batch 34): the write side confirms, the read side that surfaces it returns nothing, and the model's 'it isn't there' is TRUE. Three subsystems, one pattern — which makes it a platform question rather than three bugs.
